title: Deep learning on pretreatment ADC MRI predicts chemoradiotherapy response in rectal cancer
summary: A deep convolutional network trained on pretreatment ADC (and T2) MRI patches from 700 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, split chronologically into training (n = 500) and test (n = 200) groups, classified good responders to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy with AUC 0.851 versus 0.723 for mean ADC. Sensitivity was 94.3% and specificity 68.3%. The study is retrospective with a time-split test set and the abstract is the only source reviewed.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional neural network on pretreatment ADC and T2 MRI patches classifying good versus non-good responders

evidence.tested: Chronologically held-out test group (n = 200) with a pathology reference.
evidence.unknown: Independent-center and prospective performance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep convolutional network learned response-related features from ADC images across scanners.
